overview: The Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) requires people who lobby or do political work in the United States on behalf of foreign governments or companies to publicly register with the Justice Department, but it exempts some activities, such as ordinary commercial work and lobbyists already registered under the separate domestic lobbying law. This bill, called the PAID OFF Act, would end those exemptions for anyone working for a company or government entity owned or controlled by certain "countries of concern" already listed in State Department law. It would also let the Secretary of State, after consulting the Attorney General, propose adding or removing countries from that list, with any change taking effect only if Congress passes a joint resolution approving it. The changes would expire after 5 years. As of July 27, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it without changes and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say adversary governments use these exemptions to influence U.S. policy out of public view, and requiring full registration would make that influence transparent.
against: Critics say the added paperwork could burden ordinary businesses with ties to those countries, and that requiring a vote of Congress to update the list could make it slow to keep current.
